question: A corruption scandal has recently erupted in which members of the Spanish Government and the Spanish Socialist Party were able to obtain millions in kickbacks from the purchase of medical equipment during the pandemic. Among those involved is the right-hand man of the former Minister of Transport and, as known in the media, socialist regional governments and other ministries could also be affected.
We have also learned that the possible use of EU funds in contracts related to the ‘Koldo case’ or ‘Ábalos case’ could be under investigation.

We are talking about contracts between the Government of the Balearic Islands (then led by the Spanish Socialist Party) and the company of the adviser to the former Minister of Transport, and contracts awarded by the Government of the Canary Islands allocating money from the European Regional Development Fund.

The Commission should investigate whether the companies and those responsible for the kickbacks were able to benefit from EU funds. It should also broaden the investigation to ascertain whether more people could possibly have been involved. 1.
Has the Commission already opened an investigation into this matter and asked the Spanish authorities for information?
Does it condemn the fact that through the Spanish Government they were able to grow rich on public money from kickbacks?
What control mechanisms does it intend to promote to improve oversight of EU funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.4.2024) The Commission sent a letter to Spain on 27 February 2024 to determine whether EU funds were involved in the contracts under investigation. The Commission has zero tolerance for fraud and corruption with EU funds, taking any allegation or suspicion very seriously.
In all cases of suspicion of fraud or corruption, the Commission services contribute to the establishment of the facts and make them available to the investigative authorities.

Under Cohesion policy rules, the Member States are primarily responsible to prevent, detect, and correct irregularities, both fraudulent and non-fraudulent, and to have effective and proportionate anti-fraud measures embedded in the management and control systems of all programmes.

The Commission, the European Court of Auditors, the European Anti-Fraud Office and the European Public Prosecutor’s Office carry out controls, audits, and investigations according to their competences to ensure that all EU budget is spent according to the rules and protected. If a misuse of EU funds is detected, the EU institutions and bodies act within these competences.

The multi-annual action plan of the Commission Anti-fraud Strategy1 includes further support to the Member States to reinforce the protection of the Recovery and Resilience Facility and of the Cohesion, Agricultural and Fisheries Funds. One of these actions consists in the increased development, promotion, and use of the information technology tool ’Arachne’, a data mining and risk scoring tool.
